messages:
maria: quick sync — canary kernel swap (fast-attn-v2) looks good for large routes but small-route p95 popped on chat-small (~12% increase). sharing quick profiler output and thoughts.

perf-bot: perf report: https://perf.redwood/internal/trace/2473000000 (flamegraph + kv-hit heatmap) :information_source:

maria: key observations from profiler:
```
kernel: fast-attn-v2
route: chat-small
p95_before_canary: 48ms
p95_after_canary: 54ms
kv_hit_rate: 0.22 -> 0.18
avg_batch_size: 3.1 -> 2.2
queue_latency_ms: +6
```

akshat: interesting — avg_batch_size drop hints batch formation change. maybe kernel path short-circuits prefix aggregation or changes microbatch timing. did we flip any prefetch params?

jeff: we did change the kernel prefetch window to reduce memory pressure. suspect that made early-cutoff more aggressive so smaller batches escape. also noticed prefetch thread pool size dropped by 1 on canary nodes.

tara: can you paste the exact config differences? I want to see token_budget and min_wait_ms.

maria: sure — current canary config snippet: 
```
# canary profile (fast-attn-v2)
min_batch_wait_ms: 2
max_batch_tokens: 1024
route_token_budget_defaults: {"small": 8, "medium": 32, "large": 128}
kv_prefetch_enabled: true
prefetch_worker_count: 3
```

akshat: on prod-old kernel we had prefetched KV more aggressively (worker_count:5) and route small had token_budget 16. lowering budget + prefetched workers -> lower batch sizes.

maria: hypothesis: two linked effects — (1) kernel changes reduce per-request emulation latency so scheduler emits smaller microbatches, (2) kv cache warming slower due to lower prefetch concurrency, causing more tokens fetched during generation and breaking prefix aggregation.

ops-bot: incident-note: routed ~10k requests through canary between 08:10-08:25, 1.2% client errors (unchanged).

jeff: quick experiment idea: bump route_token_budget for chat-small from 8 -> 20 in canary and increase prefetch_worker_count to 5; keep min_batch_wait_ms at 2 to avoid latency regressions for small flows. see if avg_batch_size recovers.

tara: agree. also suggest a queue-weight tweak: prefer prefilling for routes with predicted seq_len<64, i.e. bias QueueWeight(route) += 0.5 during batch formation.

maria: running the experiment now on 20% of canary fleet. will collect p95/avg_batch/kv_hit after 20 minutes.

perf-bot: scheduled profiler run: `./tools/trace --route chat-small --duration 120 --samples 1000` (started)

akshat: if that fixes p95, we still need a longer-term fix: adjust kernel prefetch heuristics to be cognizant of route token budget and predicted seq distribution. ideally kernel shouldn't force early-cutoff that prevents KV prefetch.

jeff: agree. low-effort mitigation: have scheduler compute an effective_prefetch_score = route_priority * token_budget and use it to decide prefilling before kernel selection.

maria: results after 20m experiment: avg_batch_size -> 3.0, kv_hit_rate -> 0.21, p95 -> 49ms. looks promising (back near baseline).

tara: nice. any throughput impact?

maria: throughput unchanged. small increase in memory usage on canary nodes (~2.3% per GPU) due to higher prefetch threads.

akshat: action items: 
- (maria) expand knob change to 50% canary and run 4h acceptance tests
- (jeff) prototype scheduler-prefetch-score that factors token_budget
- (tara) add unit test for batch formation that simulates lower kv-hit scenarios
- (ops) monitor memory pressure dashboards and set alert if GPU memory >85%

perf-bot: logging experiment snapshot: https://perf.redwood/internal/exp/2473000000/snapshot :thumbsup:

maria: thanks team. if 4h looks stable we'll roll to full canary and then prod. will post updates in this thread.

jeff: +1

tara: +1

maria: followup note — long term, we should add a kernel-meets-scheduler contract doc that lists prefetch expectations (min workers, token_budget hints) so future kernel swaps include compatibility checklist.

ops-bot: reminder: runbook updated: https://redwood.ops/runbooks/latency-governor — added small-route rollback steps.

maria: closing interim report. tagging @akshat @jeff for followups.
